questions.q: What disaster has stripped the land in chapter 1?
Who does Joel tell to wake up and weep because the sweet wine is cut off?
What does Joel say the invading nation's teeth are like?
What does Joel say has been cut off from the LORD's house?
options: The meal offering and drink offering

questions.q: Joel tells the land to mourn like whom?
options: A virgin in sackcloth for the husband of her youth
A widow weeping at the city gate
A mother mourning her only son
A shepherd who has lost his flock

questions.q: Sanctify a fast. Call ____. Gather the elders to the house of the LORD.
Tell your children about it, and have your children tell ____, and their children, another generation.
LORD, I cry to you, for the fire has devoured ____.
Joel calls on the priests to put on sackcloth and mourn.
Joel says the herds groan because enemy soldiers carried them off as plunder.
Who does Joel first call to hear this word?
What day does Joel say is at hand?
What has the invading nation done to the fig tree?
options: Stripped its bark and thrown it away
Pulled it up by the roots

questions.q: What does Joel say is happening to the seeds?
All of the trees of the field are withered; for joy has withered away ____.
wrong: from the hearts of the elders

questions.q: The animals of the field pant to you, for ____ have dried up.
Joel says the wheat harvest was destroyed but the barley harvest survived.
Where does Joel say to blow the trumpet and sound an alarm?
What does God promise to pour out on all flesh?
How is the land described before and behind the great army?
options: Like Eden before them, a wilderness behind
A wilderness before them, Eden behind
Like a sea before them, dry behind

questions.q: How does the army get into the houses?
options: In at the windows like thieves

questions.q: Where are the priests told to weep?
options: Between the porch and the altar
At the gate of the city
On the steps of the palace

questions.q: Tear your heart and ____, and turn to the LORD, your God.
I will restore to you the years that ____ has eaten.
The chapter says whoever calls on the LORD's name will be saved.
God promises grain, new wine, and oil, but says Israel will stay a reproach among the nations.
God says he will bring the northern army into Jerusalem to punish his people.
How does Joel describe the day of the LORD?
options: A day of darkness and gloominess
A day of bright fire and light
A day of feasting and joy

questions.q: What does the great army's appearance look like?
What does God give the children of Zion in just measure?
How does the army march?
options: Each in his line, without swerving
Only in the dark of night

questions.q: Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. ____.
questions.answer: Your young men will see visions

questions.q: The sun will be turned into darkness, and ____, before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
Joel says even the bridegroom and the bride should come out to join the gathering.
Where does God say he will gather all nations for judgment?
Which peoples does God ask, Will you repay me?
To whom had the children of Judah been sold?
What does the chapter say will flow out from the LORD's house?
Beat your plowshares into swords, and ____ into spears.
Multitudes, multitudes in ____! For the day of the LORD is near.
Put in the sickle; for ____. Come, tread, for the wine press is full.
The chapter says the LORD will be a refuge to his people and a stronghold to Israel.
The chapter says Egypt and Assyria will become desolate for the violence done to Judah.
The chapter says strangers will still pass through Jerusalem after God dwells in Zion.
From where will the LORD roar?
The nations sold a girl in exchange for what?
Where did the nations carry God's finest treasures?
What happens to the stars as the day of the LORD nears?
Let the weak say, ____.
The mountains will drop down sweet wine, ____, all the brooks of Judah will flow with waters.
questions.answer: the hills will flow with milk
wrong: the valleys will fill with grain
the hills will flow with oil

questions.q: The chapter says Judah will be inhabited forever.
